children: An XRP Ledger maintenance amendment is running on a new activation clock after losing the validator majority behind its earlier countdown. The fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment regained majority support on October 21, moving its earliest possible activation window to November 4, subject to that support continuing.
The amendment regained validator majority on October 21 after its first countdown failed. A fresh two-week window points to November 4 at the earliest, if support holds.

At the XRPL Dashboard’s October 24, 07:09 UTC snapshot, 32 of 35 trusted validators supported the amendment, or 91.43%. The tracker showed a new majority timestamp of October 21 at 14:46:22 UTC. Those figures are a dated observation; validators can change their positions.

XRPL Win’s amendment history separately records the earlier attempt beginning October 9 and losing majority on October 21. The interrupted run lasted more than 12 days. It did not satisfy the uninterrupted period required for activation, so the earlier October 23 expectation no longer applies.

The ledger’s official amendment documentation requires support from more than 80% of trusted validators for two weeks. If support falls below the requirement, the waiting period starts again when the amendment regains majority.

Network processing also means the end of the two-week period should not be treated as an exact appointment. Amendment decisions are handled through designated ledger checkpoints. November 4 is therefore a conditional earliest window, rather than a guaranteed switch at precisely 14:46 UTC.

This is a consensus process among validators on the blockchain. Holding XRP does not itself constitute an amendment vote. The visible count matters because it shows whether the required network support is being maintained throughout the waiting period.

The official amendment description groups fixes affecting vaults, lending, automated market makers, permissioned exchange functions, trust lines, NFTs and other ledger features. Examples include more precise vault rounding and changes to when a loan can be treated as in default.

Another change concerns delegated payment permissions. The documentation says an account with a delegated PaymentBurn permission should also need PaymentMint permission to cross a zero balance into minting. That concerns issued tokens and multi-purpose tokens, which can represent tokenized assets; it should not be described as permission to mint native XRP.

The package also separates signing prefixes used for sponsor and counterparty signatures. These are changes to the handling of transactions and permissions, rather than evidence that a new lending service has launched.

Separate lending amendments still have their own voting status. Users tracking the wider DeFi roadmap should therefore distinguish the cleanup package from activation of those features. The next decisive development for this amendment will be sustained majority through the full window, followed by the ledger recording it as enabled.
Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: XRP Ledger Fix Upgrade Faces November 4 Earliest Activation After Vote Reset
